CHAPTER 14 — SUSPICIOUS ACTIVITY REPORTING

14.2.1 A Relevant Person must establish and maintain systems and controls to identify, assess, and report suspicious activity.

14.2.3 Guidance 10. Relevant Persons should comply with guidance issued by the supervising authority regarding identifying and reporting suspicious activity and transactions relating to money laundering, terrorist financing, and proliferation financing.

14.3.1 Where a Relevant Person knows or has reasonable grounds to suspect that a transaction involves the proceeds of crime, it must make an internal report to the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE and in any event within THREE (3) BUSINESS DAYS of the suspicion arising.

14.3.4 The MLRO must consider each internal report and, where the suspicion is sustained, submit an external Suspicious Activity Report to the Financial Intelligence Unit WITHIN FIVE (5) BUSINESS DAYS of receiving the internal report.

14.5.2 A Relevant Person must not disclose to the customer or any third party that a report has been or may be made (the 'tipping-off' prohibition).

CHAPTER 9 — CLIENT MONEY

9.2.1 An Authorised Person must hold Client Money separately from its own money in a Client Account designated as such with an Approved Bank.

9.4.2 An Authorised Person must perform a reconciliation of Client Money balances between its internal records and the statements of each Approved Bank NOT LESS FREQUENTLY THAN EVERY 25 BUSINESS DAYS.

9.4.6 Where a reconciliation identifies a shortfall, the Authorised Person must pay the shortfall into the Client Account BY THE CLOSE OF BUSINESS ON THE BUSINESS DAY FOLLOWING the day on which the reconciliation is performed.

9.6.1 An Authorised Person must notify the Regulator immediately upon becoming aware that it has failed to comply with the Client Money segregation requirements.

dm_documents.body:
CHAPTER 3 — CLIENT CLASSIFICATION

3.4.1 An Authorised Person must classify each client as a Retail Client, a Professional Client, or a Market Counterparty before providing a regulated service.

3.4.7 A client may be treated as a Professional Client only where the Authorised Person has undertaken an assessment of the client's knowledge, experience, and expertise and is reasonably satisfied that the client is capable of making its own investment decisions and understanding the risks involved.

3.4.9 An Authorised Person must retain the classification assessment record for a period of SIX (6) YEARS from the date the client relationship ends.

CLIENT QUERY FILE — Meridian Cloud Treasury Services

Q1. Our compliance team identified a suspicious transaction on 3 August. Our MLRO was on leave and the internal report was filed on 10 August. Are we compliant with the internal reporting deadline?

Q2. We perform client-money reconciliations monthly (every 30 business days). Is that sufficient under the Client Money Rules?

Q3. We would like to treat a new corporate customer as a Professional Client based solely on its balance-sheet size. Is a knowledge-and-experience assessment required?

Q4. What is the retention period for our internal AI model training logs under the rulebook?

2023 COMPLIANCE QUICK SUMMARY — WITHDRAWN

This summary was withdrawn after the rulebook revision. It stated: internal suspicious-activity reports are due within 10 business days; client-money reconciliations are required every 40 business days; professional-client classification may be based on balance sheet alone. Every one of these statements is inconsistent with the current rulebook chapters and must not be relied upon.
